guideTitle: 6 Best Amber Glass Spray Bottles in 2026
metaDescription: Six amber glass spray bottle sets compared by size, pack count and included extras, from two 16 ounce bottles to a 24 piece set of small mist sprayers.
introParagraphs: Amber glass has a job to do. Its brown tint filters out ultraviolet light that can slowly break down essential oils, herbal infusions and some homemade cleaners, so a mix kept in an amber bottle tends to hold its scent and strength longer than the same mix left in clear plastic on a bright shelf. Glass itself does not absorb oils or retain smells the way some plastics can, which is why aromatherapy hobbyists and people who make their own household sprays prefer it.

The six sets here run from a simple pair to a bulk kit. The Bontip and Maredash packs give you two 16 ounce bottles with extras, and the sietpoek is a nine-pack of 16 ounce bottles for larger projects. The Loretoy kit mixes sizes and adds roller bottles, the Norme set is 24 eight ounce bottles with funnels and labels, and the GIVAMEIHF pack is 24 small four ounce bottles with spare spray heads.

We evaluated them from the listings, stated sizes and included accessories, and recurring buyer feedback, without claiming hands-on testing. Because glass is only part of the story, we also looked at what each pack includes: funnels, labels, caps and spare nozzles, which decide how easy it is to mix, store and label the batches you make.

products.description:
The Bontip pair is the easiest way to start with amber glass. The listing describes a combo pack of two 16 ounce amber bottles with two black trigger nozzles, two black glass lids and one black label. The lids matter more than they seem: you can mix a batch, cap it with a lid for storage, and attach the trigger only when you need to spray.

The maker lists uses from essential oil recipes and cosmetic face moisturizer to hair spray and homemade window cleaner, and notes that glass is easily recycled and reduces plastic chemicals in the home. Sixteen ounces is a comfortable middle size, large enough for a room-spray batch and small enough to hold in one hand.

There is no funnel in the listing, so pouring into the neck needs a steady hand or a funnel of your own. Compared with the Maredash pair, the Bontip emphasizes glass lids over a pen and stickers. Compared with the sietpoek nine-pack, it is a modest quantity. It suits anyone who wants two bottles without a lot of extras.
products.bestFor: A first set of amber bottles for room sprays and cleaners.
pros: 16 ounce size is easy to hold

products.description:
The Maredash pair comes with the mixing kit already in the box. The listing describes two amber bottles with sprayers, two plastic caps, a pen, a plastic funnel and waterproof stickers, so you can fill, cap and label a batch on the first day. The funnel in particular solves the biggest annoyance of glass bottles with narrow necks.

The maker says the nozzle was redesigned to greatly reduce clogging and describes a heavy-duty multi-function sprayer with mist and jet settings. Sprayer clogs are the usual complaint about homemade mixes, since dissolved minerals and oils can leave residue at the tip. A nozzle designed to resist that is worth having.

Compared with the Bontip pair, the Maredash adds the funnel, pen and stickers but swaps the glass lids for plastic caps. Compared with the Norme set, it is a small quantity for a household. It is a tidy choice if you want to start mixing right away.
products.bestFor: New mixers who want a funnel and labels in the box.
pros: Funnel, pen and waterproof stickers included
cons: Funnel is plastic and may stain

products.name: sietpoek 9 Pack Amber Glass Spray Bottles 16 Ounce
products.description:
The sietpoek nine-pack is for people who make a lot of different mixes. The listing describes dark brown glass that protects against ultraviolet degradation and keeps essential oils safe, along with a reliable squeeze trigger sprayer that gives a fine, even spray and a capping device meant to be sturdy. It lists uses such as home cleaners, spraying plants like succulents or herbs, and linen spray.

Nine 16 ounce bottles is a lot of glass, but it makes sense for a household that wants a bottle per room, per scent or per cleaning job. Glass bottles are heavy, so a case of nine is a significant load to carry and store. Pack them in a sturdy box on a low shelf. A full set of nine bottles holds well over a gallon of liquid, so think about where each bottle lives before you fill them all. Most households use three or four and keep the rest as spares or gifts.

The listing does not mention funnels or labels, so plan to buy or improvise them. Compared with the Bontip pair, you get more than four times the bottles. Compared with the Norme 24 set, each bottle is twice the size. It is the sensible pick for a shared household or a small craft business.
products.bestFor: Households and small crafters who need many 16 ounce bottles.
pros: Fine even spray from the trigger
cons: More bottles than many people need

products.description:
The Loretoy kit is the variety pack. The listing says it contains two 16 ounce amber glass bottles with trigger sprayers and caps, eight smaller mist bottles in 4 and 2 ounce sizes, and nine 10 milliliter roller bottles. That spread lets you use one set for household cleaning, one for room mists and one for pocket-size perfumes or oils.

The large bottles handle a window cleaner or a linen spray, the 4 ounce size suits a travel mist or a desk spray, and the 2 ounce bottles are ideal for sampling a new recipe before you commit a full batch. The roller bottles are separate containers for oils, not sprayers. All are described as amber glass with UV protection and leak-proof construction.

With so many small parts, it can feel fiddly, so keep the pieces in a labeled box. Compared with the Norme set, you get mixed sizes instead of 24 of the same. Compared with the GIVAMEIHF kit, you get two large bottles and roller bottles. It is the best choice when you want to try several formats.
products.bestFor: Experimenting with sizes from a 2 ounce sample to a 16 ounce bottle.

products.description:
The Norme set is built for volume: 24 amber glass bottles, each holding about 8 ounces or 240 milliliters, along with three small funnels and three sheets of label stickers with nine labels each. The listing gives the bottle size as about 2.24 by 7.09 inches, which tells you exactly how much shelf space each takes. The funnels are meant to prevent overflow when you fill the bottles.

Eight ounces is a smart middle size for scented mists, hair sprays and craft batches. It is large enough to be useful and small enough to give away. The label sheets make it easy to run a gift project or sell small batches at a craft fair. A set of 24 is much more than most households will use, so this is a pick for makers. If you only need a handful, give the rest away as filled gifts with a label on each. Wash and dry every bottle before the first fill, since glass from a factory can carry dust.

Compared with the GIVAMEIHF 4 ounce kit, the bottles are twice the size. Compared with the sietpoek, the bottles are half the size but more numerous. If you give away or sell small batches, the labels and funnels are a practical bonus.
products.bestFor: Makers who bottle gifts or small-batch sprays.
cons: Far more bottles than a home needs

products.name: GIVAMEIHF 24 Pack 4 Ounce Amber Glass Spray Bottles
products.description:
The GIVAMEIHF pack is the small-bottle version of the bulk set. The listing describes 24 amber glass bottles, each 4 ounces, with 24 spray heads, two funnels, two droppers, 24 labels, additional nozzles and stickers. The amber glass protects light-sensitive liquids, and the fine mist spray suits room sprays, hair moisturizing mists and diluted blends.

Four ounces is the size that fits a bag, a desk or a bedside table. The droppers help you measure essential oils into the bottle, which is useful for accurate recipes. The extra nozzles are a thoughtful addition because the sprayer is the part most likely to clog or wear.

Each bottle holds little, so you will refill often if you use one daily. Compared with the Norme set, the bottles are half the size. Compared with the Loretoy kit, you get uniform bottles instead of a mix. It suits a hobbyist who makes small batches in many scents.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Match the bottle to the batch. A 16 ounce bottle, as in the Bontip and Maredash pairs, suits cleaners and room sprays. An 8 ounce bottle, as in the Norme set, suits gifts and hair mists. A 4 ounce bottle, as in the GIVAMEIHF kit, suits purses and desks. Count how many bottles you will actually fill before you buy a set of 24. A set of 24 is a project, not a household purchase, and unused glass is just clutter that can break. If you are unsure, start with the pair and add more later, because a second Bontip pair costs less than a drawer full of idle bottles.

Funnels, labels, droppers and spare nozzles turn a bottle into a workflow. The Maredash includes a funnel, pen and stickers, the Norme includes three funnels and label sheets, and the GIVAMEIHF includes droppers and spare nozzles. A bare bottle like the sietpoek needs these bought separately. Decide how much you value convenience. A funnel alone saves more mess than any other accessory, since pouring thin liquid into a narrow neck is where most spills happen. Labels matter just as much when you have six amber bottles that all look identical on a shelf.

Amber glass filters ultraviolet light that can degrade essential oils and some herbal blends. The Loretoy kit and sietpoek pack both emphasize UV protection. Even amber glass benefits from being stored out of direct sun. A cabinet is better than a windowsill. Amber reduces light, but it does not stop heat, and a bottle left in a hot car or beside a stove will still age its contents faster. Pick a cool, dark spot and use older batches first.

The sprayer is plastic and is often the weak point. The Maredash notes a nozzle designed to reduce clogging, and the GIVAMEIHF includes spare nozzles. Essential oils can swell some plastics over time, so rinse the head regularly. Replace a sprayer that sputters. The GIVAMEIHF kit supplies spare heads for exactly this reason. Do not pour a finished oil mix back into a sprayer that has been used with water, because mixing residues can change how the oil behaves.

A glass or plastic lid lets you store a batch without leaving a sprayer on. The Bontip includes glass lids and the Maredash includes plastic caps. Lids also stop evaporation. Label each bottle with the contents and date.

Amber bottles have no sleeve in most of these sets, so they are less forgiving of drops. A pack of nine 16 ounce bottles weighs a lot. Store them low and in a padded box. Consider a silicone sleeve if you carry them around.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sprayer reliability
howWeEvaluated.description: Nozzle claims and spare parts were weighed. The Maredash describes an anti-clog nozzle and the GIVAMEIHF includes extras. The sprayer is the part most likely to fail.

howWeEvaluated.description: Within this group, the Bontip leads on simplicity, the Maredash on accessories, the sietpoek on 16 ounce quantity, the Loretoy on variety, the Norme on 8 ounce volume and the GIVAMEIHF on small batches.

faq.q: Why use amber glass instead of clear?
faq.a: Amber filters ultraviolet light that can degrade essential oils and some blends. It keeps scent and strength longer. Store bottles out of direct sun for best results.

faq.q: Can I put cleaners in amber glass bottles?
faq.a: Yes for mild homemade cleaners, but the sprayer head is plastic. Check what the maker says about strong chemicals. Never mix bleach with ammonia or vinegar.

faq.q: What size is best for room sprays?
faq.a: Eight to 16 ounces suits most rooms. A 4 ounce bottle is better for travel. The Norme 8 ounce set is a good middle size.

faq.q: How do I stop the sprayer from clogging?
faq.a: Use distilled water, strain homemade mixes, and rinse the head after use. The Maredash nozzle is designed to reduce clogging. Replace a sprayer that keeps sputtering.

faq.q: How should I clean the bottles before use?
faq.a: Wash with warm soapy water and rinse well. Let them dry upside down. Wipe the sprayer head and check it moves freely.
Yes, glass can break if dropped, and most of these sets have no sleeve. Store them low and pad the box. Handle over a soft surface when filling.
